newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee tightly mixed, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee tightly mixed, seen consolidating.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures see-sawed on overhead trade selling and industry buying at the lows before ending the day tightly mixed. Traders said conditions were dull.
"There's not a lot going on today," said one trader. "There's light industry action in both London and New York but there's nothing to shout about."
Traders said the market was seen moving sideways possibly in consolidation phase after recent price volatility.

Benchmark May traded from a low of $1,513 a tonne to a ceiling of $1,545 before settling the day just $5 down at $1,530. Chart-wise, May is seen supported at $1,500 while on the upside, the immediate target is pegged at $1,570.
Front-month March was also active and prices finished off lows at $1,509, a $8 loss.
March/May spread widened slightly to $21 at the close from Friday's $16 finish with the March contract coming under selling pressure ahead of the first delivery day next week.
Traders said news warehouse workers at Brazil's key Santos port began strike on Monday over a dispute over backpay had no significant impact.
"I don't think there will be any impact (on the market)," said one trader. "There are only around 140 workers said to be involved in the strike."

But union officials said on Sunday although only about 140 workers were involved, the stoppage for an indeterminate period was expected to bring 90 percent of all import activity and 70 percent of export activity at the port to a halt.
But a spokeswoman at the port said on Monday the stoppage would affect imports but not exports.
Santos is a major export outlet for Brazilian commodities including coffee.
Other major news over the weekend included Colombian coffee industry's forecast that 1996/97 crop would certainly be below 11 million, possibly to a low of 10.4 million.
Brazil meanwhile said it would have to draw on its official coffee stocks currently standing at 13.2 million bags to meet demand at home and abroad. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
